@torch.no_grad()
def sample_causal_candidates(
    seq: torch.Tensor, positive: torch.Tensor, itemnum: int, count: int = 32
):
    """Uniform replacement draws excluding only the visible prefix and target.

    Stable sorting makes the first matching item carry its earliest position.
    Thus membership tests do not exclude items occurring only in later positions.
    No quadratic catalog mask or B x L x K x L tensor is constructed.
    """
    batch, length = seq.shape
    positions = torch.arange(length, device=seq.device).unsqueeze(0)
    sorted_items, original_positions = torch.sort(seq, dim=1, stable=True)

    def first_occurrence(values):
        shape = values.shape
        flat = values.reshape(batch, -1).contiguous()
        index = torch.searchsorted(sorted_items.contiguous(), flat)
        index = index.clamp_max(length - 1)
        found = sorted_items.gather(1, index).eq(flat)
        first = original_positions.gather(1, index)
        return found.reshape(shape), first.reshape(shape)

    _, first_input = first_occurrence(seq)
    unique_prefix_count = (seq.ne(0) & first_input.eq(positions)).long().cumsum(1)
    found_target, first_target = first_occurrence(positive)
    target_in_prefix = found_target & first_target.le(positions)
    available = itemnum - unique_prefix_count - (~target_in_prefix).long()
    valid = seq.ne(0) & positive.ne(0)
    eligible = valid & available.gt(0)
    skipped = (valid & ~eligible).sum()
    negatives = torch.randint(1, itemnum + 1, (batch, length, count), device=seq.device)

    def rejected(draws):
        found, first = first_occurrence(draws)
        prefix_hit = found & first.le(positions.unsqueeze(-1))
        return (prefix_hit | draws.eq(positive.unsqueeze(-1))) & eligible.unsqueeze(-1)

    bad = rejected(negatives)
    for _ in range(8):
        number_bad = int(bad.sum().item())
        if number_bad == 0:
            break
        negatives[bad] = torch.randint(1, itemnum + 1, (number_bad,), device=seq.device)
        bad = rejected(negatives)

    # The bounded rejection stage keeps dense-prefix cases from stalling.
    # Both accepted rejection draws and fallback draws are uniform on A.
    if bool(bad.any().item()):
        catalog = torch.arange(1, itemnum + 1, device=seq.device)
        for b, t in bad.any(dim=-1).nonzero(as_tuple=False).tolist():
            allowed = catalog[
                ~torch.isin(catalog, seq[b, : t + 1]) & catalog.ne(positive[b, t])
            ]
            mask = bad[b, t]
            n = int(mask.sum().item())
            indices = torch.randint(allowed.numel(), (n,), device=seq.device)
            negatives[b, t, mask] = allowed[indices]
    return negatives, eligible, skipped

def sample_training_candidates(history, positive, itemnum, count=32):
    """Unique uniform negatives excluding the complete training history.

    This runs inside the user-aware sampler. Held-out interactions are never
    consulted. Zero slots are padding and must be masked from candidate CE.
    """
    seen = np.unique(np.asarray(history, dtype=np.int64))
    seen = seen[(seen >= 1) & (seen <= itemnum)]
    pool_size = itemnum - len(seen)
    result = np.zeros((len(positive), count), dtype=np.int64)
    positions = np.flatnonzero(positive)
    k = min(count, pool_size)
    if not len(positions) or k == 0:
        return result, pool_size

    # Each next-item target belongs to the complete training history.
    if not np.isin(positive[positions], seen).all():
        raise ValueError("Training target missing from complete training history")

    allowed = None
    if pool_size <= 4 * k or len(seen) > itemnum // 2:
        allowed = np.setdiff1d(
            np.arange(1, itemnum + 1, dtype=np.int64), seen,
            assume_unique=True,
        )
        draws = np.stack([
            np.random.choice(allowed, size=k, replace=False)
            for _ in positions
        ])
    else:
        draws = np.random.randint(1, itemnum + 1, size=(len(positions), k))

        def rejected(values):
            order = np.argsort(values, axis=1, kind="stable")
            ordered = np.take_along_axis(values, order, axis=1)
            duplicate = np.zeros_like(values, dtype=bool)
            duplicate[:, 1:] = ordered[:, 1:] == ordered[:, :-1]
            bad = np.zeros_like(duplicate)
            np.put_along_axis(bad, order, duplicate, axis=1)
            return bad | np.isin(values, seen)

        bad = rejected(draws)
        for _ in range(8):
            n_bad = int(bad.sum())
            if n_bad == 0:
                break
            draws[bad] = np.random.randint(1, itemnum + 1, size=n_bad)
            bad = rejected(draws)
        if bad.any():
            allowed = np.setdiff1d(
                np.arange(1, itemnum + 1, dtype=np.int64), seen,
                assume_unique=True,
            )
            for row in np.flatnonzero(bad.any(axis=1)):
                draws[row] = np.random.choice(allowed, size=k, replace=False)

    result[positions, :k] = draws
    return result, pool_size
